reasoning: Read to the end, the turn carries several acts and no act absorbs another. 'Where was the readme sample?' is a question: answer it with the link, create nothing. 'Always give the link if I forget' settles a standing rule with force beyond this message, so it is a decision recorded separately from any work item. 'Wait, project-B will give you an idea, pick it up, but meanwhile keep working' plus 'are you working?' is a status question and an instruction to continue what is already running; the project-B idea has not arrived, so there is no goal to state and no row is opened on the hope of one. 'Give a plan, time measurements, write everything' is the one instruction that names a result nothing already covers: a plan asked for is something to be made, work like any other, so it earns a decision sheet and one new piece of work. 'We leave the cafe in an hour but you definitely have an hour, then I will relaunch from home' names that a limit is close and says how the work resumes; that is an observation the work should be paced by, not a correction, since it drops no requirement and adds no step. Nothing running is stopped, so there is no halt, and no in-flight goal changes, so nothing attaches to existing work. The only dimension that genuinely changes is documentation and communication: the plan and its time estimates get written down. No specialist is needed; routing a plain request for a plan to the communicator instead of doing it is how the request disappears.
